Subject: Question on cluster sizing & ramp windows

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to finalizing our internal budget and procurement timeline for the recommendation engine and conversational assistant. A few follow-ups from our infra team:

- We expect a launch traffic peak around mid-November (approx 2.5M queries/day).
- P50 latency target 120ms on generation paths, P95 under 300ms.
- We need a committed minimum GPU reservation to satisfy our internal SLAs for Q4 and a clear ramp schedule for additional capacity as usage grows.

Can Redwood propose: (1) a minimum cluster size you’d recommend to meet targets with safety margins, (2) a 90/180-day ramp schedule with cost tiers, and (3) any mandatory minimum-term commitments?

Also, Rajiv (copied) will handle procurement.

Best,
Elena Morris
Head of Platform, Wellness Plus

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@wellnessplus.ai>

Elena —

Super helpful context, thank you. I’ve looped in Jonas (solutions) and Marcus (sales-engineering) to validate sizing assumptions. High level answers below; I’ll attach a concise proposal + quote after we align internally.

Proposed options (quick summary):
1) Minimal committed cluster (Conservative): 8x A800 GPUs with 2-worker redundancy (effective capacity = 6 active workers) — good for beta and bursty traffic; meets P95 under 300ms for 99% of gen workloads.
2) Production baseline (Balanced): 16x A800 GPUs with auto-burst to 24 GPUs via capacity pool — recommended for steady-state 2.5M q/day with caching and batching optimizations.
3) High-throughput (Aggressive): 32x A800 (or mixed A800+H800 depending on model) for peak elasticity and lower token cost.

Ramp schedule (suggested):
- Day 0-30: Provision baseline (option 2) at 50% throughput (8 GPUs active, remaining reserved).
- Day 31-90: Grow to 100% baseline (16 GPUs active), monitor KPIs and add burst capacity if 7-day MAU growth > 15%.
- Day 91-180: Conditional add rule to scale to option 3 if traffic transits above 3.5M q/day for >10 days.

Commitments: 12-month reserved plan recommended for pricing stability; quarterly review + canary rollouts funded by Redwood for the first deployment wave.

I’ll wait for Jonas to confirm the min GPU guarantee and Marcus to include a cost delta for different commitment levels.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Soojin / Elena / Rajiv —

Quick engineering confirmation and constraints:

- Model profile: We assume a mix of a 7B open decoder for embeddings + reranking and a 13B LLM for generation. Baseline perf numbers: 13B on A800 -> ~16 tokens/sec per GPU under optimized kernel path.

- Minimum guaranteed active GPUs: Redwood can commit to a minimum of 10 active A800-equivalent GPUs (this covers steady-state 2.5M q/day with prefix caching across sessions) under a 12-month reserved contract.

- Safety margin: We recommend reserving an additional 20% headroom in the committed pool to account for traffic spikes and model changes (so effectively 12 GPUs guaranteed for SLA math).

- Ramp mechanics: We support time-based ramp (pre-provision reserved instances over weeks) and traffic-based ramp (auto-burst policy to access shared burst pool). For procurement simplicity, we propose:
  * Phase 1 (0-30 days): 10 committed GPUs active; 6 reserved standby for immediate warm-up (total reserved = 16).
  * Phase 2 (31-90 days): 16 committed GPUs active; 8 reserved standby (total reserved = 24).
  * Phase 3 (91-180 days): scale to 24 active as-needed; option to convert standbys to active as traffic persists.

- Pre-warm and model pinning: Pre-warm KV caches and pin a model variant per route to reduce cold-starts — adds ~10% additional warm GPU usage for the first 48 hours of a rollout.

Notes about cost tiers: converting reserved standbys into active GPUs mid-term has a conversion fee (covers GPU re-provisioning and priority scheduling). We’ll include explicit numbers in the quote.

Attachment: I pushed a short cluster_plan.xlsx (capacity rows + example cost table) to the thread.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
(Attachment: cluster_plan.xlsx)
